Prevention: Use certified seed to reduce the chance of contamination.
Seeds are transported by water - construct contour bunds, box ridges and water ways to prevent water runoff from infested land to clean fields.
Seeds travel on machinery - clean farm equipment soon after work in infested areas.

Use trap crops such as cotton, sunflower and dicholos beans to deplete the seed bank.
Plow under or harvest before parasite emergence or seed set as they are very long-lived.
Practice crop rotation with a non-host crop, such as a non- leguminous crops like maize, sorghum or cassava.

Monitoring: Annual herbaceous broadleaved plant, 30-45 cm high; single hairy stem, or sometimes branched near soil level.
Always growing in association with host plant.
Flowers pale yelllow, sometimes with three deep red veins.
Leafy when flowering, resembling free- living plant.
Inspect fields bi-weekly and take control measures to avoid flowering and seed set.
Direct Control: Prevent seed set by hand pulling before flowering in lightly infested fields, particularly if there is no history of previous infestation.
Immediate ploughing of crop residues after harvest to prevent continued seed production.
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.

Pre-emergence herbicide mixtures containing pree (metazachlor+ antidote) according to manufacturer's instructions
